'''''Alopecurus aequalis''''' is a common species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known as '''shortawn foxtail''' or '''orange foxtail'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> It is native to much of the temperate Northern Hemisphere from Eurasia to North America. It is most commonly found in areas near fresh water, such as the margins of ponds and ditches.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alopecurus aequalis {{!}} Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora|url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/alopecurus-aequalis|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.brc.ac.uk|language=en|archive-date=2021-05-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527121424/https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/alopecurus-aequalis|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Description==
This perennial [[bunchgrass]] is variable in appearance. It produces bunches of erect stems between 20 and about 70 centimeters in height.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Alopecurus aequalis (Shortawn Foxtail): Minnesota Wildflowers|url=https://www.minnesotawildflowers.info/grass-sedge-rush/shortawn-foxtail|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.minnesotawildflowers.info|language=en}}</ref> The leaves are 2–15 cm long; the basal leaves are the longest and the few stem leaves are long-sheathing.<ref name=":0" /> The cylindrical [[inflorescence]] is a few centimeters long and blooms with white to yellow to bright orange [[stamen|anthers]] about 0.5-0.8 mm long.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alopecurus aequalis in Flora of China @ efloras.org|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200024817|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.efloras.org}}</ref>

The leaf blades are narrow, about 1–8 mm wide. The flowers are attached to branches, rather than the main axis of the inflorescence.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alopecurus aequalis (short-awned meadow-foxtail): Go Botany|url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/alopecurus/aequalis/|access-date=2021-05-27|website=gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org}}</ref>

==Ecology==
''A. aequalis'' has a [[C3 carbon fixation|C3 metabolism]], grows best in full to partial sun, and can tolerate shallow standing water for up to two months during the growing season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Short-Awned Foxtail (Alopecurus aequalis)|url=https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/sa_foxtail.html|access-date=2021-05-27|website=www.illinoiswildflowers.info}}</ref>

One variety of this species, [[Alopecurus aequalis var. sonomensis|var. ''sonomensis'']], is a rare [[California]] [[Endemism|endemic]] grass which is federally listed as an [[endangered species]] of the United States.<ref name="USFWS">{{cite web|url=http://ecos.fws.gov/docs/federal_register/fr3169.pdf|title=Determination of Endangered Status for Nine Plants From the Grasslands or Mesic Areas of the Central Coast of California|work=Federal Register|publisher=United States Fish and Wildlife Service|access-date=November 6, 2013|date= October 22, 1997}}</ref>
